text:
anya: Heads-up — ran an end-to-end perf pass on the AWQ int8 path and found a new micro-regression tied to the calibration sampler hitting the packing hot path repeatedly. numbers look small per-request but add up at scale :grimacing:

mike: ugh, can you paste the profile? is this during cold-start or steady-state?

anya: steady-state with long KV lifetimes. main symptom: kernel chooser flips between weight-only pack/unpack kernels rapidly because calibration sample variance changes group-size heuristics. causes extra memcpy/pack ops. snippet: ```
[PROFILE] model=redwood-awq-int8 v=3.2
batch=8 seq=1024 avg_latency=43ms -> 53ms (+23%)
pack_time_avg=3.1ms pack_time_p95=12.7ms
kv_lookup_hits=0.98 kv_evictions=120/min
kernel_switches=42/min
```

sadiq: so calibration sampling is non-deterministic and done per-request? that sounds wrong. i thought we did calibration once per model load and cache the quant params.

anya: historically yes, but we added a "sampling-per-batch" mode to get better group-size estimates for mixed-seq workloads. the sampler uses a small random prefix slice and then recomputes group centroids which feeds kernel-selector.

jen: that mode was to handle very skewed token distributions, but if it triggers kernel churn it defeats batching. can we memoize sampler output for the session or at least decay decisions? :thinking_face: 

anya: my proposal: keep the per-batch sampler but only apply changes if the estimated throughput win > X% and stable for N consecutive windows. fallback to cached calibration otherwise. also add a cheap fast-path that avoids full re-packing if only a small fraction of groups changed.

mike: concrete numbers for thresholds? we need to avoid increasing p95 during bursts. maybe require 3 consecutive windows and a >=5% token-level latency win.

anya: agreed. i prototyped a heuristic: require delta_throughput >= 6% and stability_count >= 2 windows (each window 30s). cheap patch added: `if changed_groups < 12% then skip repack` — that reduced extra memcpy by ~70% in the microbench.

perf-bot: Regression detector alert: model=redwood-awq-int8 v=3.2 latency p95 increased 19% in canary over baseline. Trace id: cb1f2a.

sadiq: can this interact with KV cache evictions? if KV gets thrashed we do extra token re-encodes which touch pack hotpath again.

anya: yes — logs show bursts of KV evictions around the same time as kernel switches. likely memory pressure + new pack routines causing transient evict/resync. we should instrument a counter linking kernel_switch->kv_invalidations.

jen: for the quick fix: 1) revert sampler to session-cached mode for canary; 2) add the cheap `changed_groups` skip; 3) in parallel, add an infra metric for kernel_switches and kv_evictions so SRE can alert. can we ship this today?

mike: can do revert + skip as a patch deploy. jen, sadiq — can you own metrics + alert? i'll coordinate the canary rollback plan.

infra-bot: deploy queued: revert-awq-sampler-session-cache patch -> canary cluster. ETA ~25m.

anya: thanks. after the rollback I'll run the longer AB run with the sampler-stability filter and post numbers. long-term we should consider doing sampling offline at compile/upload time for deterministic kernels and storing per-tenant calibration artifacts.

mike: +1 on storing calibration artifact. also add a small TTL so model updates retrigger a re-calib.

sadiq: one more idea — use a lightweight bloom-ish sketch to estimate group distribution cheaply instead of full sample clustering. much less CPU and no pack. could avoid churn entirely.

anya: interesting, i'll prototype a sketch-based estimator. will report back in this thread with microbench numbers. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
